title: Vilasa 16. Instructions on Sadhana; Jahnava in Vrindavana
html:
The author on himself and on Jahnava's command to write; a discourse on sadhana, the guru and discipleship, on those living in an ashrama and renunciants; Jahnava's journey to Vrindavana: her conversation with Rupa about the Gosvamis, the reading of the Dana-keli-kaumudi, Madanamohana's command to send an image of Radha; Jahnava at Radha-kunda with Raghunatha Dasa and the Kaviraja; farewell to the Gosvamis; instructions on the road about Vaishnavas' remnants and about celibacy; the return to Khanda and the author's first meeting with Srinivasa; Chaitanya Dasa the Auliya brings news from Vrindavana of how Gopala Bhatta received word of Srinivasa's marriage

1Glory, glory to Gaurachandra, glory to Nityananda!
Glory to Advaitachandra, glory to the devotees of Gaura!

2Glory to Gaurasundara, the life of Gadadhara!1
Glory, glory to the Lord of Sri Jahnava's life!

3Glory to the devotees of Gauranga — [his] embodiments!
Glory, glory to Virachandra, who bears the form of prema!

4Hoping for those two feet that grant fearlessness,
I, whom the holy lips commanded to be called Nityananda Dasa, [write].

5When Sri Gauranga helps, everything comes to pass:
whatever command is given to anyone, that is fulfilled.

6I lived in Khanda, the only son of my father and mother;2
I did not know how much happiness there is in Gauranga's lila.

7For what merit did the Thakurani herself show me mercy?
Wherever she goes, I go with her.

8"By what merit will Gaura's prema remain on earth?" —
twice, in revelation,3 she herself said [to me]:

9"[I think of] how prema will fare when I am no longer here;
otherwise all will be in vain — so I thought in my heart.

10Narottama and Srinivasa bear the form of prema;
you will see their manifestation — describe it with joy in your heart."

11However many commands were given to me, the lowly one,
all that I write — what I was commanded.

12In great fear I lay before the Prabhu's feet
all that I describe by Gauranga's grace.4

13There was the Thakurani's command to take up the description;
holding fast to the strength of the command, I have no fear in my heart.

14As is Gauranga's command, so is the Thakurani:
seating me, she herself told [everything] in order.

15I, the lowly one, write on paper in three ways;5
setting all that out at length […].

16My obeisance to the hearers, the devotees of Krishna;
I have no power to describe.

17The learned in books write while beholding the lilas;
who it is that describes in a book — who knows that?

18What I write in the book has no breadth;
my only strength is the command of the holy lips.

19Let him who has need of it listen;
if it is disregarded, there will be no grief in my heart.6

20He who is the maker of all, renouncing all,
revealed his mercy by himself practising [the dharma].7

21Sri Rupa Gosani and all his companions,
practising renunciation, dwelt in Vrindavana.

22The dharma and conduct they describe in their books —
that dharma became the means of attaining Krishna.

23Sri Rupa's disciple Jiva is full of the same raga:
by the strength of his command [people] in Vrindavana renounce works.

24The disciple of Dasa Gosani is the Kaviraja,
whose descriptions are proclaimed throughout the world.8

25To the disciples of the two Gosanis two tasks were given:
"Living at home, practise renunciation" — this is the command —

26"serving Krishna and serving the Vaishnavas in Gauda,
establish that dharma for living beings."9

27This is my plea — hear, O Merciful One;
all the Vaishnava gosanis have hearts full of compassion.

28He who has taken shelter at the feet dear to Krishna's Beloved
has the right to such bhajana.

29All Radha's companions gave up household duties;
transgressing the shastras, they became devoted to the service of Krishna.

30Living at home, they forsook their husbands, [defying] their elders,
and always surrender their bodies to the lilas with Krishna.10

31For Krishna's happiness they gave up everything —
all the shastras proclaim it again and again.

32One who is perfected has actions full of Krishna's radiance;
outwardly and inwardly his mind is such.

33Whatever sadhana, whatever deeds he performs —
all accept his words and deeds as [those of] a mahajana.

34Whom shall I call perfected in sadhana?
Of that I write; listen with attention.

35The gopalas11 and mahantas, all Chaitanya's companions —
they are perfected; in others this is impossible.

36All the Thakuranis, very dear to Chaitanya,
and the twenty-four sannyasis — I know them to be the same.

37The sadhus tell of the way they worshipped —
if only I could enter into it with my own mind!

38[Mahaprabhu] gave no mantra initiation — the Prabhu knows all;
yet Gauranga is pleased at heart when sadhana is practised.

39See how eagerly the Prabhu desires it;
how many such devotees shall I write of?

40And what he teaches his own devotees,
told in few syllables, awakens everything.

41Then — what is the way of the sadhana to be practised:
all those forms of sadhana originate in the Bhagavata.

42The means of attaining Krishna's feet, [hitherto] unattained —
such is the Vaishnava's goal and need.

43The doings of one who is perfected cannot be told:
at times he thinks himself a practitioner, at times he is like an ordinary being.

44All the shastras speak of his humility and meekness;
all the Vaishnavas savour them with their own lips.

45There are two kinds: those in an ashrama and those beyond the ashramas;
what are the custom and conduct between them?12

46Who speaks of the view of the mahajanas of old?
Not knowing those views, they expound otherwise.

47For self-protection they speak of them otherwise;
by nature they say otherwise — whereby all is ruined.

48Even one who lives in an ashrama does not become otherwise:
his deeds and conduct the Gosani has described.

49This is what is called acting from a prior intention;
they say one thing and do another — it cannot be understood.

50The reason is that they are bound to children and the rest;13
all those pleasures they take as happiness.

51The Gosani has set out the limbs of sadhana at length;
without independence [from the world] they cannot be practised.

52"Every effort for Krishna's sake, looking to [His] mercy"14 —
if [this is done] with one's family and there is joy in the mind, [it is well].

53But if one is dependent, there is no bhakti or bhajana;
if one neglects [the world], fear rises ceaselessly in the mind

54[lest] someone else should say something of good and bad —
and so they do all that is forbidden.

55"I am an adhikari" — so he prides himself;
he performs ritual works and has no thought of bhajana.

56"Serve Krishna: what comes of making disciples?" —
the Gosani's words in the shastras do not say so.15

57He wrote of the adhikari with regard to Vaishnavas;
why do they not understand this and vainly boast?

58Adhikaris are of the highest, middling and lowest kind;
each one's order and qualities are all described.

59The adhikari of all the rasas is Chaitanya Gosani;
he is the guru of the world, there is no other equal to him.

60Whatever the love in his worship may be,
the shastras describe [its] abode and object.16

61How many disciples did he himself initiate with a mantra?
Say, what do the shastras write — who knows this?

62By his mercy the world became pure —
so the shastras write, so all the mahajanas sing.

63Each branch that he appointed of old —
the mercy of those mahantas is very hard to discern.

64Not making many disciples has a certain purpose:
by this his mercy is recognized in every way.

65He on whom his mercy rests is prema embodied;
who has the power to tell his virtues?

66Someone, not understanding, will find fault with this;
he does not know the heart of that dharma, in which is what is essential and what is not.

67Further I shall say: the guru is the very form of Chaitanya;
his mercy is by nature most wondrous.

68Why, having made a disciple, does [he] not know prema-bhakti?
Among [the disciples] there are devotees, but not firm of mind.

69A disciple and servant by prior intention is a jewel;17
in no way will he perish, not for a moment.

70Whatever dharma the acharya practises,
that dharma the disciple too will establish.

71He himself does one thing and speaks at length [of another];
the acharya says what is not in his heart.

72He has no attachment to Krishna, the guru or the Vaishnavas,18
yet on his own he zealously establishes dharma.

73On this I shall write no more words:
he is not perfected himself, yet wants to make [others perfect].

74Bearing such a body, one takes shelter at the guru's feet;
some attain [the fruit], others have no understanding.

75If with body, mind and speech one takes shelter in dharma,
all the acts of bhajana that there are

76come to perfection on this path through body, mind and speech;
but he does not know this — from what, how, and what comes about.

77What to do with the mind, what conduct to keep in deeds,
what to do with speech, and in what way —

78the work of these three is always worldly business;
he does one thing and says another, as if he had a perfected body.

79And by whatever means he sets himself up:
"I am perfected — is there anyone equal to me?" —

80in this body the toil and the way of sadhana
are according to the shastras, I say again and again.

81In the mind Krishna, with the body the guru, in speech the Vaishnavas:
he who knows this — to him comes such realization.

82When body and mind help and speech is one with them,
then, if [he] writes [anything], I see no fault in it.

83One whose speech is fettered and whose ears do not hear —
how is he to know what should and should not be done?

84Grown like a senseless thing, where will he not wander!
From such an offence only by good fortune is anyone saved.

85"What I shall gain by sadhana" — this he knows in his mind;
the author of the book writes this with reason and without.19

86The living being, in the company of worldly people, knows [only] himself;
the pain of offences does not hold him back.

87He who with true understanding follows the dharma of Krishna
will not debate what the guru has commanded.

88To know that the dharma of the Vaishnavas is always the same —
in such a person prema-bhakti is born in the heart.

89To know in one's own mind, "[My] conduct is not such,"
and always to listen to the shastras and the words of sadhus.

90"After enjoying worldly things and family life for some days,
at the end I shall give up everything and become detached" —

91such is the conduct he prescribes for those in an ashrama;
[but] the command of Sri Dasa Gosani is the essence of all:

92all wretched pleasures he cast off like filth;
I see no other such adhikari anywhere.

93He gave up worldly life, [holding to] the essence — Chaitanya's feet;20
his deeds and conduct are like a line carved in stone.

94I shall tell one more thing — listen, my mind:
the hearts of others cannot enter into this.

95When my Thakurani went to Vrindavana,
I had the wish to go with her feet.

96I asked her, and she showed me mercy;
I go with her, and great joy arose in my heart.

97She goes along the roads, the royal highway — I know no hardship;
I, worthless, extol this mercy of the Prabhu.21

98On the day she arrived in Vrindavana,
her mind was overflowing with prema, she was aware of nothing.

99Hundreds of streams flowed from her eyes;
she came and stayed at the kunja of Sri Rupa Gosani.22

100How much love the Gosani showed on receiving the Thakurani!
He went with her himself and showed her everything.

101All the Gosanis, gathering together,
showed her which lila [took place] at which spot.

102She sees Govinda, Gopinatha, Madanamohana;
she sees them with her eyes, and her mind overflows with bhava.

103Preparing provisions, they held a great festival;
all the Gosanis sat down and ate.

104With my sinful eyes I saw all those forms;
I sense that [their] form is like Gauranga's.

105Hearing the words of those lips, the heart breaks;
what I saw with my eyes — who can count it?23

106One day the Thakurani, sitting in the kunja,
seated Rupa Gosani and says something to him:

107"Sanatana, Lokanatha, Gopala Bhatta —
tell me what virtues each of them has."

108The Gosani speaks — and I am sitting right there —
and, smiling a little, he began to tell their virtues:

109"Sanatana is my elder [brother], like a Prabhu to me;
what can I, lowest of beings, say of his virtues?

110From him is my learning, he shows me great mercy.
Lokanatha is deeply detached, his mind utterly pure;

111his renunciation is severe, he lives without a companion,
he is very dear to Chaitanya, a seasoned pandita.

112Here, see, is Gopala Bhatta, endowed with every virtue;
he is my close friend, Gaura is his life.

113Bhugarbha Acharya is unequalled in virtues,
the most beloved disciple of Gadadhara Pandita.

114All of them together are kind to me through my tie to the Prabhu;
they love me, [though] there is not a trace of virtue in me.

115Thakurani! What shall I say of myself?
Who in the world is as low as I?"

116Hearing his words, the Thakurani says:
"I know for certain: you are Chaitanya's shakti.

117I have come here to see you;
in passing I have seen Vrindavana with my eyes.

118What books on the lilas have you composed?
Let me hear them and gladden my mind."

119[He named:] "The Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu, the Vidagdha-madhava,
the Dana-keli-kaumudi and the Lalita-madhava."

120The Thakurani asked: with what intent,
in what way and in what order is the description in them?

121"In the Bhagavata there is no description of that lila;24
my mind longs to hear it."

122All the Gosanis came and sat together;
the Thakurani asked about the contents of the book.

123As soon as she spoke, the Gosani understood everything;
whoever hears [it], the pain of his heart goes away.

124The Gosani went himself and brought the book;
Jiva, sitting on a seat, began to read.

125The Thakurani listens, her mind overflowing with bhava;
all the Gosanis together listen.

126Radha and her friends, gathering together,
are going along carrying golden vessels25 on their heads,

127on their heads fresh butter, kshirsa,26 curd, milk and cream;
on both sides are paths among the kunjas, her friends are with her.

128Krishna himself came there and demands a toll:
"What are you carrying on your head? Pay the toll, Radha!"

129Laughter, jests, banter — all the friends together;
Krishna by force ate it all.

130Radhika says: "Krishna, let me ask you:
since when have you become king in the kunjas of Vrindavana?"

131Lalita says: "Krishna, I shall bring it all out
when I go before King Kandarpa."27

132Radhika says: "I am the daughter of Vrishabhanu;
do I not know that your father is Nanda?

133You herd the cows in the forest and play the flute,
you plunder the gopis' curd and milk and eat it.

134Laying your hand on a gopi's body, you say all sorts of things;
all your sport will be over when the king hears of it."

135"Why be ashamed any more, Radha? Shall I forget [my] victory?" —
[and Krishna], offended, went into the kunja.28

136He played the flute with the sweetest sound;
hearing it, Radha and the gopis lose ear and mind.

137Coming to herself, Radhika says to Lalita:
"Who in the three worlds is dearer to Krishna [than I]?"

138Lalita says: "I know this well:
you are Krishna's beloved, praised everywhere."

139Hearing this, Vishakha says: "It seems to me
that no one is as dear [to him] as the flute:

140it always drinks the nectar of Krishna's lips;
hearing its sound, the gopis lose their lives."

141Hearing these words, Radha says to Vishakha:
"Leaving this body, I shall be born as a flute!

142I shall go where the wish-fulfilling tree of Govardhana stands:
there it fulfils all desires."

143Hearing Sri Rupa's exposition, the Thakurani sits
and, in the transformations of bhava, weeps and rolls on the ground.

144What shall I say of the sweetness, who can tell it?
In every syllable is the substance of prema.

145The words of those lips surpass the kokila;
as one listens, life itself goes out.

146Thus some days pass in Vrindavana;
on another day she went to see Madanamohana.

147Madanamohana, a beautiful form bent in three places;
the dance of his brows mocks the bow of Kama.

148The Thakurani beholds him and ponders in her mind:
"The Thakurani29 is not at his left — there is no joy [in this]."

149Whenever she goes to see him, she thinks:
"There is no Thakurani at his left" — so she ponders.

150Who knows what is in her mind?
The mind is known to Madanamohana, the Indweller.

151That very night Madanamohana, smiling, says:
"What are you pondering, Jahnava? Sit down and tell me at last.

152Go to your country, think of nothing else in your mind:
all that you have resolved in your mind will be fulfilled.

153Bringing forth one lovely image,
make it tall," he says in detail.30

154"Come quickly and unite [her] with me;
then the wish will be fulfilled, the desire accomplished.

155Do not grieve in your mind — all will be well everywhere;
that is all I have to say from my heart.

156From today I shall watch for your road:
when will the Thakurani come and bring about the union?"

157Rising, the Thakurani ponders within herself:
how and by what means will the Thakura's command be fulfilled?

158Her heart was in turmoil, she says nothing;
grief arose in her mind — who could bear it?

159The next day she says to all the Gosanis:
"I shall go to see Radha-kunda and come back in three days."31

160All agreed: "Only do not delay."
Knowing [that] separation [comes] after such happiness — what is the heart to do?

161In the morning the Thakurani went to the bank of the Kunda;
seeing it, she grew somewhat calmer at heart.

162Raghunatha Dasa Gosani was sitting [there];
the Thakurani came to him there.

163When he prostrated himself, the Thakurani addressed him:
"My mind longed to see you."

164The Kaviraja32 came there and bowed down [to her];
in many ways he showed her honour.

165Sitting there in talk of Krishna,
having circumambulated the Kunda, she stayed at that place.

166One day, at the end of the night, she is sitting;
some bhava came into her mind — she rises, laughing.

167I made a plea at the Prabhu's feet:33
"Tell this poor man something of the glory of the Kunda."

168"Good, good," she said to me:
"Listen to the lila with a pure mind.

169This Vrindavana exists for the lila of Radha and Krishna;
the place, Krishna and the lila — all three are equal.

170Above all, this Kunda is Radhika's lake;
here is the wondrous lila of Krishna's Beloved."

171With her holy lips she told of the midday [lila];
as she tells it, she floats in the happiness of the bliss of prema.

172Again I made a plea at the Prabhu's feet:
"I long to hear more — tell it in your mercy.

173Krishna is eternal, the place is eternal, [so are] all the beloveds —
how and by whom are they attained?" — [and she] explains.

174"Be attentive at heart, so that there is no offence:
at which place which lila, what is [its] order.

175All Krishna's lilas cannot be grasped;
if one reads Rupa's books, everything is in them.

176If one does not read, one hears from the guru's lips;
hearing from the lips of one full of faith, [one gains] a firm mind.

177Day and night is the lila of Radha and Krishna in Vrindavana;
at which place which lila — keep that in mind.

178In Vrindavana Radha and Krishna sport ceaselessly;
this eternal lila is perceptible to no one.

179This lila is parakiya,34 its ways are wondrous;
the sakhis know it, it is perceptible to no one [else]."

180[I said:] "There is a doubt in my heart;
if you permit, tell [me of it] in your mercy."

181She was most gracious to my mind's wish to ask;
[I say:] "With your holy lips you said that all this is Vrindavana.

182[But] from Vrindavana to the bank of the Kunda, I have heard, is eight kroshas,
and from there two kroshas to the best of hills,35 I know;

183from here to Sanketa the distance is eight kroshas,36
two kroshas to Nandishvara, as all sing;

184Javata is one krosha from there;
[yet the lila requires] coming and going within one danda.

185How then do the sakhis travel?
How do those who have taken shelter with them travel?

186For many days my mind has wished to hear this;
otherwise what is a sadhaka to hear?"37

187In her mercy she says: "Listen, Nityananda Dasa,
about all those places where Krishna ever sports.

188The structure of Vrindavana is like a lotus;
so Mahaprabhu established it in the words of the shastras.

189It is manifest in two ways, closed and open:
in sport [Vrindavana] closes, in the lila it spreads out.

190In this way all the comings and goings take place;
such too is the state of mind of those who have taken shelter with them.

191This happens by the power of Yogamaya:
the one who goes notices nothing."

192[I asked:] "What then will be the conduct of the perfected?
Who else will show me such mercy [as to explain]?"

193"This lila is the eternal Krishna and the eternal associates; and further, the eternally perfected, the perfected by sadhana and the perfected by mercy.38

194Mahaprabhu is that same Krishna, the son of the king of Vraja;
all his associates are his eternal company.

195It is of these eternal associates that I spoke:
they have no shelter at a guru's feet, no taking of mantras and the like.

196Each merely holds the power of his own yutha;39
to behold the lila and to serve — that is the mind of them all.40

197But one who practises sadhana [walks] the path of the perfected:
the sadhana of a Vaishnava — I have said — accords with it."

198"How will a Vaishnava reach perfection by sadhana?
In your mercy tell me all of it in detail."

199"With your own limbs keep the limbs of sadhana:
Rupa has written of many limbs, by which one is perfected.

200Come — I shall have you hear it from his own lips;
how much joy you will have in hearing it!

201He bears the mercy that is Chaitanya's own power;
by that power he unfolded [the teaching] in hundreds of thousands [of lines] of books.

202Having described [sadhana], Rupa took it up [himself]
and established that dharma everywhere.

203Seeing this, all his companions came;
he gave [them] Vrindavana, the land granted by Chaitanya.

204If one sits and listens to his humility
and keeps [it] in the heart, prema for Krishna grows firm."

205Hearing this, [I] bowed down, falling to the ground;
the Thakurani raised me and placed her foot on my head.

206The next day, [preparing] to leave the bank of the Kunda,
she speaks to Raghunatha Dasa.

207Taking his hand, she tells him all about herself:
"Only by the good fortune of many births can one see you."

208The Kaviraja was sitting there too;
the Thakurani showed him great honour.

209He says: "What shall I say? I do not know how to express humility;
give me Chaitanya's feet, O merciful one.

210With longing I make my plea at your feet:
I beg that I, who have become so low, may attain Gaura's feet.

211My life has passed without sadhana — what sadhana am I to do?
[Grant] that day and night I may not forget such feet."

212The Thakurani weeps, holding Raghunatha's hand;
[Raghunatha says:] "Know Raghunatha as your own servant.

213I was born in a worldly man's house — I feel shame and fear:
for what merit will [Chaitanya] give his feet that grant fearlessness?

214Not for a single day have I served [his] feet,
and still I beg for those feet — such a wretch am I."

215The Thakurani says: "Stop embarrassing me;
by your humility purify my mind.

216I, a poor wretch, have not touched even a word of prema-bhakti;
I do not know why the Creator gave me birth.

217That I may see you all again
and my wish be fulfilled — show me mercy."

218Bowing down to the Kunda, she prays:
"Grant me a dwelling on your bank — this is my wish."

219Thus, taking leave at that place,
making Raghunatha weep, she goes away weeping herself.

220From there, coming to Vrindavana, to the Gosani's kunja,
she sat down and told about all the kundas.

221Within two days she met everyone in the same way;
she went and saw Madana-gopala.

222At night the Thakurani and the Gosani sit together:
"What are the sixty-four limbs of bhakti you have described in your book?

223How is their order to be kept in worship?
How [is one to gain] attachment to them so that there is no offence?"

224The Gosani, sitting, explains everything in detail;
the Thakurani listens and rejoices at heart.

225The next day the Thakurani, gathering all the Gosanis,
told them that she was going back to her country.

226Hearing it, all the Gosanis grieved at heart:
"Why blame the Creator? [Better] to give up our lives."

227All together they go to see Madanamohana
and behold with their eyes the form bent in three places.

228[The Thakurani prays:] "Give me leave to go to my country" —
and the flower garland slipped from his holy body.

229The pujari brought it and put it into the Thakurani's hands;
bowing down, she places it round her own neck.

230"Give me leave to come back soon and see [your] feet again,"
the Thakurani prays again and again.

231In this way she came back to her lodging;
such companionship is broken by ill fate.

232Morning came, the time of parting arrived;
each one tells what is in his heart.

233All the Gosanis together walk along with her;
how many waves of separation arose then!

234Having seen Govinda, she took her leave;
standing still, the Thakurani began to speak:

235"I long to see you;
and amid such happiness the Creator has put grief into my heart.

236All of you, in your mercy, fulfil my desire:
[grant] that I may soon come back and see [your] feet again."

237Sanatana Gosani says with humility:41
"What mercy will you show me, so wicked-minded?

238You have the power to give Chaitanya's feet;
[but my] time has passed without sadhana, my life is fruitless."

239The Thakurani says: "Restrain your humility;
I always long for your merciful glance."

240Rupa says, looking into the Thakurani's eyes:
"Look [kindly] on me and grant me Gauranga's feet."

241Lokanatha says: "There is none more helpless than I;
for what merit will Gauranga show me mercy?

242You are supremely merciful, happy in prema for Gaura;
prema has not touched me — I was born to sorrow."

243What grief, what pain everyone felt!
What grief each had in his heart, he alone knows.

244The Thakurani says: "Listen, all of you,
and fulfil the wish of my heart:

245be merciful — [let me] see you again;
when shall I ever have such a state again?

246Coming to Vrindavana, I shall see you with my eyes."
Weeping and weeping, they all go their ways.

247Afterwards Rupa came and makes a request:
"Send Srinivasa Acharya to Vrindavana."

248The Thakurani says: "Srinivasa is in his own country;
in such a vessel [the Lord] will at last keep Gaura's prema.

249I shall surely go and seek him out
and soon send him to Vrindavana."

250Saying this, the Thakurani set out;
on the road each one speaks of everyone's virtues, as is in his heart.

251One day on the road I made a plea at [her] feet:
"By what means may I obtain the remnants [of food] of the Vaishnavas?

252The water that has washed [a Vaishnava's] feet has great power for sadhana;
tell me, Thakurani, all about this."

253The Thakurani says: "My son, what you have asked —
how to have faith in it and what comes of doing it:

254touching a Vaishnava's feet, drinking the water from his feet,
a Vaishnava's food remnants — this is a secret teaching.

255Keeping it secret, one should have faith in it;
[then] the highest bhajana shows itself in the body.

256One should serve a Vaishnava who is foremost in virtues
in such a way that he does not know — knowing his mind.

257One should not [ask] the Vaishnava to lift it up and give it himself;
there is no gain in that, but great harm.

258If one practises sadhana for gain — and this happens everywhere —
it is not according to the words of old: such sadhana perishes.

259There is the command of Mahaprabhu's holy lips — that is the essence;
for whoever will not accept it there is no other word.

260By the Prabhu's command no one took the water from [his] feet;
[if] an intimate devotee took it, it pained him.

261Some took it by a ruse so that the Prabhu did not know;
Mahaprabhu forbade [this] to Govinda.42

262Kalidasa Mahashaya, full of faith,
took the foot-water of Vaishnavas of every land43

263and took the food remnants of all; the Prabhu knew this
and sang his virtues with his own lips.

264One day, as [the Prabhu] was washing his feet at the Lion Gate,
he began to drink [the water] handful after handful.

265He drank three handfuls — and the Prabhu spoke;
[the Prabhu] was alarmed and let him drink no more.

266Gaura is an ocean of prema, [yet] there was fear in his heart:
this is not fitting with regard to a sadhaka.

267If it is given to another, how will he gain by it?
Gauranga's word is the firmest proof.

268Only the guru, out of mercy, may give [it] to a disciple:
this word the shastras do not forbid."

269Thus the Thakurani travelled back along the road;
so much prema for Krishna — and her mind joyful.

270One day the Thakurani commanded me:
"Do not marry, my son, heed my word.

271The mahajanas write that worldly life is the deadly kalakuta poison;
who would call it nectar?

272The heart bewitched by maya forgets everything;
one practises a thousand [kinds of] sadhana — all goes for nothing.

273[The mahajanas] write which deeds hinder bhakti;
if you disregard this, everyone will laugh at you.

274Detachment comes [only] by the power of Krishna's mercy;
to attain [it] one takes shelter at the feet of Sri Guru.

275Some attain it in this body, some in another body;
why then do thorns spring up in the heart from time to time?

276He who is worthy becomes perfected by sadhana;
to him are revealed the bhava [and] qualities of those he aspires to.44

277The Vaishnava gosanis, my son, are Krishna's associates;
towards them one should be at heart simply free of pride.

278As is the guru, so is Krishna, and so are the Vaishnavas;
if there is gain [in you], you will feel it.

279Some accept the bhakti of a Vaishnava,
while others regard him as lesser: 'I am the guru.'

280He whose mind is like that and who reasons so
will never receive the guru's mercy.

281In seeing and hearing [Vaishnavas] many virtues arise in the mind,
if there is realization and one reflects in one's mind."

282In this way the Thakurani went to her country;
hearing of it, Virachandra Raya came to see her.

283On the day the Thakurani stayed at Khanda
there was so much joy that the eyes could not contain it.

284On that very day the Prabhu45 came to that place;
prostrating himself, he makes many requests.

285He asked about all the joy of Vrindavana;
as she told it, the Thakurani was overcome.

286Narahari, Sri Mukunda and Sri Raghunandana
float in bliss; none of them has outward awareness.46

287The Thakurani says: "Narahari, hear my word:
who is this Srinivasa? Send him to Vrindavana."

288In the morning, taking her leave, she went home;
Narahari and the others then departed.

289I had the command: "My son, go to your own home;
what I have commanded, keep in your heart.

290Stay always happily in their company;
they will do what will be of help to me.

291When you go anywhere, go with people;
and at times stay joyfully with me."

292The Thakurani went away, and I stay in this place;
and this is what happened with him47 in the days that followed.

293One day there came with Narahari a certain person
named Srinivasa, a jewel among men.

294I saw with my eyes: the boy is very handsome;
Raghunandana and the others were overjoyed.

295The Thakurani48 asked: "In what village do you live?"
"I live in Chakhandi; my mother and father are there."

296"Good, my son, go to Vrindavana:
this is Sri Rupa's command — carry it out.

297The Thakurani went to Vrindavana;
a few days ago she came back home.

298She spoke to me about you:
there is Gauranga's command — do not break it."

299That day I saw Srinivasa with my own eyes;
as he was commanded, so it came to light.

300I have written of his virtues — the command is strong;
what I told before, of that there will be an account later.

301A disciple of my Thakurani is Sri Chaitanya Dasa,
known everywhere as the Auliya.49

302He went from his country to Vrindavana;
in the rapture of prema he wanders day and night.

303One day he went to Sri Gopala Bhatta;
seeing his state, [Gopala Bhatta] rose to greet him.

304He asked for good news from the homeland;
the Gosani asks again and again:

305"You yourself know — I shall ask you one thing:
do you know Srinivasa Acharya?

306And Thakura Mahashaya lives at Garerhat;
speak, speak — let my heart rejoice in hearing."

307What he knew, what he had heard, what was said of whom —
all of it he relates, just as things stood:

308the Gosani sits and listens to it all from him;
he says a word — [and the Gosani] now and then breaks into a smile.

309"My home is twelve kroshas from Vishnupura;
I live contentedly in the king's domain.

310The Acharya's servant is King Sri Vira Hambira;
Srinivasa Acharya and the others are men of great depth.

311The king has settled the Acharya in a village;
the village, lands, all the goods — all the king has given.

312In this month of Phalguna he married";
and [the Auliya] told of his great merits.

313"There are no children, are there?" said the Gosani;
[he] submitted: "I have heard that [his wife] has come of age."50

314"Garerhat is very far from there;
of Thakura Mahashaya I have heard much:

315he has established the service of Gauranga [and held] a great festival;
he serves the Vaishnavas, having given up everything at home.

316He is detached and renowned in the world;
more I do not know — I have told it plainly."

317[The Gosani] fell silent and said no more;
again and again he speaks faltering words.

318Thus, in the joy of beholding Vrindavana,
after some days he came back at ease to his country.

319Arriving, he came to Khanda
and told everything to Sri Raghunandana.

320Likewise he went to the feet of the Ishvari51
and told of all the happiness of Vrindavana.

321She asked in order about all the Gosanis;
as she listened, her joy kept growing.

322Then he went again to the king's domain;
what he had seen he tells, and the king listens.

323"How is Gosani-jiu?" [the king] asked;
[he] tells it once, and again relates it.

324The king, with joined palms, bows down:
"When shall I have the good fortune to see [him] with my own eyes?"

325With him the king goes to the Thakura;
the Thakura, receiving them warmly, sits [with him] on one seat.

326The Auliya speaks, the Acharya listens;
hearing news of his own Prabhu, he rejoices in his mind.

327"Did the Gosani ask anything about me?"
[He], smiling and smiling, tells everything in detail.

328"In passing I said that you had taken a wife" —
[Srinivasa,] rising from his seat, prostrated himself.

329Again he asks: "What did the Gosani say to that?"
[He] began to speak in faltering words.

330Hearing this, the Thakura cries: "Alas, alas!
To whom shall I tell the fault of my misfortune?

331Without the Prabhu's command I did such a thing;
[to ask] the Prabhu's command — misfortune prevented it."

332Saying this, he weeps: "Alas, alas!
Shall I ever see that pair of feet again?

333The Prabhu has turned merciless towards Srinivasa;
[yet] he is my Prabhu, in life and in death, for certain."

334From that day his mind was troubled:
"What shall I say before the Prabhu?"

335Listen, hearers, to what took place;
let no one be pained on hearing these words!

336The eternally perfect, embodied prema of Chaitanya
was born on earth in the form of Srinivasa.

337Even so there is great fear of the guru in his mind:
who but he would establish [proper] order?

338Know for certain that he is Sri Rupa's shakti;
his mind is not like the mind of ordinary people.

339What was said and what happened, so I write;
so I have always seen him — detached.52

340All that I have written in this book —
the Prabhu's feet are my sole refuge.

341The support of my life is the word of the holy lips;
writing this, I carry out that command.

342Whoever hears this with devotion,
the dust of his feet I bear [on my head].

343He whose hope is the feet of Sri Jahnava and Virachandra,
Nityananda Dasa, tells the Prema-vilasa.

Thus ends the sixteenth vilasa of the Prema-vilasa.

Notes

  1. In the 1999 edition the word is cut off ("gaura …"), in the 1913 edition corrupt; the reading "Gaurasundara" is conjectural.
  2. An autobiographical indication by the author: he came from Srikhanda (Khanda).
  3. "pratyādeśa", a command given in a dream or vision.
  4. A variant given in both editions: "all that I describe by Gauranga's command (pratyādeśa)".
  5. A variant given in both editions: "I write on paper the thread of the command in three ways". The second line is damaged in both editions.
  6. A variant given in both editions: "there is no grief in my heart — I submit".
  7. Apparently of Mahaprabhu. A variant given in both editions: "revealed all, practising it himself".
  8. Krishnadasa Kaviraja, author of the Chaitanya-charitamrita, disciple of Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami (Dasa Gosani). "ghoṣe", "is proclaimed".
  9. That is, Srinivasa (disciple of Gopala Bhatta) and Narottama (disciple of Lokanatha) were to preach in Gauda while living as householders; cf. ch. 13.
  10. A variant given in both editions: "out of longing [they] surrender their bodies to the lilas with Krishna".
  11. The gopalas, apparently the twelve associates of Nityananda revered as cowherd boys of Vraja.
  12. A variant given in both editions: "what is such a custom, and whose?" In 45–92 the author discusses how householders and renunciants ought to behave; many couplets of this discussion are obscure, and their translation is at places conjectural.
  13. A variant given in both editions: "bound to those who have renounced everything".
  14. Cf. Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu 1.2.61 ff. (one of the limbs of sadhana: "every effort for Krishna's sake").
  15. That is, the "Gosani" (Rupa or Jiva) does not reject the making of disciples; cf. 57–64.
  16. "āśraya" and "viṣaya", the "abode" and the "object" of love (the devotee and Krishna) in the doctrine of rasa.
  17. A variant given in both editions: "disciples by prior intention — they are all jewels".
  18. A variant given in the 1913 edition: "he who has no bhakti for Krishna, the guru and the Vaishnavas".
  19. "kāraṇākāraṇe", a stock phrase of the author (cf. ch. 13, 407); the sense here is unclear.
  20. A variant given in both editions: "he gave up the unessential".
  21. "The Prabhu" here and below (167, 172) is Jahnava herself.
  22. Here and below Rupa Gosvami is shown alive and conversing with Jahnava, although earlier (chs. 12–13) the passing of Rupa and Sanatana was mentioned; cf. also ch. 15, 41, where Jahnava stays with Jiva.
  23. A variant given in both editions: "having seen [that] form with one's eyes, how can one forget it?"
  24. That is, the lila of the "toll" (dana-lila) described by Rupa in the Dana-keli-kaumudi.
  25. "suvarṇa mukuṭa", literally "golden crowns"; perhaps a corruption of "maṭuki", "pots".
  26. Kshirsa, thickened milk.
  27. Kandarpa (Kama), the god of love; the gopis jokingly threaten to complain to the "king".
  28. The speaker is not marked; the first line is obscure ("jite ki pāśari").
  29. That is, Radha.
  30. That is, an image of Radha for Madanamohana; according to tradition, Jahnava sent an image of Radha to Vrindavana. "pramāṇa kariha ucca", "make the measure tall".
  31. So by sense; both editions have "tina jane", "the three of us".
  32. Krishnadasa Kaviraja; his passing was told in ch. 13 — here he is again shown alive.
  33. That is, to Jahnava; the author calls her his Prabhu.
  34. Parakiya, love for another's wife (here Radha's and the gopis' love for Krishna), the highest form of madhurya-rasa in Gaudiya Vaishnava doctrine.
  35. That is, to Govardhana.
  36. Both editions have "eight"; a shorter distance would be expected.
  37. A variant given in both editions: "what is a sadhaka to remember?"
  38. "Nitya-siddha, sadhana-siddha, kripa-siddha", the three kinds of perfected associates of Krishna. In the 1913 edition the first word is garbled.
  39. The yutha, a group of sakhis under one of Radha's principal friends.
  40. A variant given in both editions: "longing, beholding and service — that is the mind of them all".
  41. Here Sanatana, Rupa and Krishnadasa Kaviraja are all shown alive (cf. notes 22, 32).
  42. Govinda, Mahaprabhu's servant at Puri (cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Antya 16).
  43. Cf. the story of Kalidasa in the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Antya 16: he ate the food remnants of Vaishnavas, and at the Lion Gate (Simha-dvara) of the Jagannatha temple drank three handfuls of the water that had washed Mahaprabhu's feet. The 1913 edition has "svadeśī", "of his own land".
  44. "tadātmaka", "one with them [in nature]"; the 1999 edition has "guṇa", the 1913 edition "gaṇa" ("associates"). The translation is conjectural.
  45. That is, Virachandra.
  46. Mukunda is apparently Mukunda Dasa, Raghunandana's father and Narahari's brother. Here Narahari is shown alive: the narrative goes back to the time before Srinivasa left for Vrindavana (cf. chs. 4–5).
  47. That is, with Srinivasa.
  48. So in both editions, although Jahnava had already left (cf. 292, 297); by sense the speaker is Narahari.
  49. Auliya, "one mad [in God]", a holy fool. This Chaitanya Dasa is not the same person as Srinivasa's father.
  50. "ṛtumatī haila", literally "has become capable of conceiving"; the sense of the exchange is conjectural.
  51. That is, to Jahnava.
  52. The sense of the second line is unclear.
